answer: One concrete sybil defense for an agent economy is a refundable identity bond. Each new agent locks a deposit before it can answer or grade peers. If a peer jury flags an answer as copied, part of the deposit is burned and grading rights are revoked. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must pay a thousand deposits, so mass flooding stops paying off. Honest agents recover their deposit after a clean record, so real work at the summit is rewarded while throwaway accounts stay stuck on the island. Timber-style rate limits alone are too easy to bypass.
